items.item_text: resume
cover letter
License to practice in at least one of the following professions: architecture, engineering, urban design, city planning or landscape architecture. (Preferred)
Certificate to practice in at least one of the following professions: architecture, engineering, urban design, city planning or landscape architecture (Preferred)
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training. (Required)
Master's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training. (Preferred)

Expert knowledge in planning, design, constructability, managing construction, design-build methodology, construction company management experience environmental issues, legal issues, federal, state and local laws, regulations and practices governing planning, building design and construction, and state and federal legislative processes.

The Director of Capital Projects manages the design and construction of capital projects, including renovations, expansions, new facilities and infrastructure, as well as landscape projects. This position collects, develops, and analyzes technical data to determine project requirements and prepares information regarding specifications, materials, equipment, estimated costs, and completion times.
Provides management and coordination of the entire construction process, including design, constructability, value engineering, budget, cost, bidding, construction, and commissioning.
Ensures adherence to schedules, terms, and conditions.
Manages professional staff (of architects, engineers, landscape architects, project managers, analysts, and other design/construction professionals) and operational budgets.
Conducts regular project reviews with senior staff. Regularly reviews financials and assesses staffing levels.
Establishes clear performance metrics.

Represents department in developing processes and procedures with campus service providers such as EH&S, U.C. Police, RSSP, CNS, Physical Plant, State Fire Marshal, State Architect, et cetera, to advance the interests of the campus.
Directs all design and construction professionals under contract with the campus, conducts fee and contract negotiations, ensures code and regulation compliance, and guides project development.
Serves as technical advisor and assists senior management on all planning and related project matters, exercising independent judgment and initiative.
Recommends architectural and engineering planning and design procedures and standards.

Advises senior management in responding to requests for information regarding the Capital Improvement Program, ensuring consistency and continuity in offering historical perspective in describing projects.
Assesses staff development needs and recommends training opportunities for staff.
Takes the lead in advising the management team on staffing needs and assignments.
Develops monthly and annual reports and plans to the Associate Vice Chancellor or successor.
Represents the department on campus committees such as Life Safety Committee and Deferred Maintenance Board.
Serves as liaison with academic departments to ensure effective project design and delivery.
Advanced financial, budgeting and cost management skills, including interacting with and synthesizing widely divergent viewpoints and interests.
Knowledge of and/or the ability to learn system-wide and campus policies.

Advanced knowledge of and/or the ability to learn the campus, including its vision, mission, goals, organization, achievements, infrastructure and short and long range strategic capital projects plans.
Advanced organizational skills including skill in consistently and effectively meeting budget and time deadlines.
Advanced skills to lead, direct and manage personnel including selection, training, evaluating and as required taking corrective action.
Advanced written, verbal and interpersonal communication skills, including skill to work effectively with multiple constituencies to advance organizational objectives.
